implementation_notes: WCF's Message class is a framework-owned envelope: the reference documents its structure as a SOAP envelope consisting of a body plus an optional Headers collection (transmitted) and a Properties collection (processing-level annotations that never go on the wire); CreateMessage builds the wrapped form and GetBody<T>() unwraps it at the destination. The same split is provided by modern transport SDKs - Azure Service Bus ServiceBusMessage (Body + ApplicationProperties) or System.Text.Json's JsonExtensionData when the envelope rides inside the body. Hand-write an envelope class only when the wire format is dictated by a legacy peer.
pitfalls: A Message is forward-only and fixed at creation: reading the body twice without CreateBufferedCopy first throws InvalidOperationException - buffer it before reading it in more than one place.
Message and the channels that own it hold unmanaged resources and are IDisposable; not closing them leaks sockets and handles.
Headers are serialized and therefore bound to the SOAP version they were created with, while Properties are not transmitted at all - putting metadata in the wrong collection silently drops it.
